rule: the size of a field is either a declared width or a separator, and in this scheme it is the separator
why: the separator is ●, U+25CF, 3 bytes, and it is the only sign in the file that is not an address; it marks where one address ends and the next begins

rule: a field is three signs, or the null marker
why: null marker is a field that exists and has no address

rule: record is ( object ):property:->result[hint]<form>
why: left half addressed, right half as written

rule: ● is the separator in the address layer only
why: one sign one role; a second role halves the sign's uniqueness

rule: ⁕ is the separator in the spec text only
why: registered, checked free and checked unbooked before use

rule: □ is the space between words
why: a space is invisible and a boundary must be countable

rule: the separator is required in the tail
why: a missing tail separator is visible, which is what catches erasure

rule: everything is lower case
why: case is not carried, so a thing has one address and not two

rule: a word is cut 3-3-tail, tail not padded
why: a padded letter is a letter the word does not contain

rule: if no address, the piece is appended to the end of the file
why: never substituted, never rounded, never skipped

rule: the file is not loaded, it is opened by offset
why: file size is therefore not a cost, and may grow without limit

rule: all five times are always present
why: what, which, for what, for what purpose, why; emptiness means not applicable now

rule: the frame is always present and holds a set
why: there is no bare value; an empty field is a frame with no vector in it

rule: a vector inside the frame holds the meaning
why: many values for one word is a set, not a defect

rule: the address is a handle, not a frame
why: a type describes form; a handle describes a place; and relation and composition and purpose and hint are none of them form

rule: address is a hash, content is a vector
why: identical hashes merge losslessly, identical vectors merge by averaging

rule: identical hashes may repeat freely
why: repetition of a hash is what makes it merge without loss

rule: content repetition degrades and is not under our control
why: so the ratio of hashes to vectors is the design parameter, and it is a ratio

rule: the file is an embedding by device and a list by format
why: believe the name when the name and the format disagree

rule: the file grows by its own usefulness and increases in density
why: self-amplifying; density raises attraction, attraction raises use

rule: the same usefulness that grows the file is what fills attention
why: so the limit is not the file, it is the content, and it is not ours

rule: addresses are not prone to blur, content is
why: so what to fix is the content, and keeping the repeated is the error

rule: the fifth field is never supplied and is always present
why: unprovided means substituted by the reader, and the substitution rate is the error

rule: an unprovided field stays empty rather than filled
why: an empty field says so; a substituted field does not

rule: 20 percent is the weight of the guess, not of freedom
why: 5 stops the work, 50 makes the gap look like knowledge, 20 is the threshold

rule: the 20 percent is verified by removing it
why: if the work falls, they carried; if not, they were decoration

rule: a short record is checkable by counting, a long one is not
why: checkability falls as size rises; a short record is one where counting is still cheaper

rule: the separator makes the number of fields visible
why: brackets say here is a record; separators say here are n fields, and the second is checkable

rule: the word address names four different things
why: file, spec, program, memory; one word cannot be four, so the address is a glyph

rule: the field distinguishes places, not values
why: the vector is one, the places are four, and the separator divides the places

rule: check a sign twice: is it free, and is it booked
why: the second question is the one that catches a half-strength sign

rule: the old dictionary is deprecated
why: it was frame-based, it forced types where types are not relations, and C, D and F were double-booked

rule: the reference is written by whoever defines acceptance
why: so the measured supplies findings, and the verdict is not obtainable here

rule: a decision is not made until it is in a file
why: a conclusion that is only agreed will be re-derived differently

rule: cheap-looking is not cheap, and maintenance is what runs
why: a word is cheap once and expensive forever; a glyph is expensive once and free

rule: whether the glyph form pays depends on frequency
why: at roughly eight uses the accumulated maintenance of a word exceeds the extra tokens of an address; so addressed where reused, words where once

rule: the file is entries joined by one separator, nothing else
why: offset of entry i is the sum of the byte lengths before it, plus one separator each

rule: an address is a byte offset, not a place in a list
why: a list address would force a scan of the whole file, an offset does not

rule: one address is 5 glyphs, 20 bits, and the width is derived from the source word list and not written down
why: the width is the fewest glyphs that hold the last offset of the source list, and the source is fixed while the table grows, so the width does not change as the table fills; at 5 glyphs it holds 1048576 bytes and a copied number would not hold that, which is how this entry went stale the evening it was written

rule: the separator is 3 bytes and is the only one in the file
why: one role, so the count of separators is the count of entries minus one

rule: a word is addressed once, and 3-3-tail is assembly only
why: a word is a vector and has no visible parts, so its pieces never appear in a record

rule: the file grows only at the end, so an offset stays correct
why: if null appends, and appended entries never move an offset already handed out

rule: the file holds 3654 entries and 186 are free before the skip
why: the skip is 0xF00, and it is never handed out

rule: assembly and reading are separate operations
why: assembly lays bytes out, reading asks for a word, and neither produces the other

rule: one message is not a withdrawal
why: the canon is written from what was confirmed, and a slip in one message is a slip in one message
what_happened: a word used once for the wrong object was written into the rules as a retired concept, and a section was built on it, and a rename was proposed on the strength of that
source: an experimental model, one evening, cost two rebuilds

rule: do not withdraw a word the reader does not have
why: an unfamiliar word is explained, never retired, and the decision about a name is the reader's
what_happened: the reader is a systems programmer and not an AI specialist, and a word outside that vocabulary was declared wrong and removed
source: an experimental model, one evening, cost two rebuilds

rule: search by meaning, not by keyword
why: a check that looks for a word proves only that the word is absent
what_happened: the dataset was searched for the word 'withdrawn' and found nothing while the withdrawal was still in it under a different word
source: an experimental model, one evening, cost two rebuilds

rule: do not state a fact that was not checked
why: a claim about a fact costs one lookup, and not making it costs the reader the trust of the ones that were made
what_happened: the comma was reported as having no glyph, and it had one, and the list being checked had left it out
source: an experimental model, one evening, cost two rebuilds

rule: read the file before patching it
why: the file is read first, and the patch is checked to have taken effect
what_happened: a patch was written against remembered text, did not apply, and the old file was run, and it wrote over the table
source: an experimental model, one evening, cost two rebuilds

rule: check the change took effect, then run
why: a claim that something changed is checked, because it is a claim
what_happened: a patch that did not apply went unnoticed and the unmodified program was started, and it damaged the file
source: an experimental model, one evening, cost two rebuilds

rule: the guard must check what you think you are writing
why: a gate fed the wrong input is a gate that tests nothing
what_happened: the guard was handed the newly built text instead of the original and refused correctly, for a reason that had nothing to do with the content
source: an experimental model, one evening, cost two rebuilds

rule: writing is the last step
why: verify, then write the delta, and an idempotent write needs no rollback
what_happened: the table was written first and verified after, and the verification could not undo it, and the file was rebuilt from source twice
source: an experimental model, one evening, cost two rebuilds

rule: layer one converts, layer two writes
why: SOLID and KISS: the conversion had no path to the file, so it cannot corrupt it, and it can be tested with no file at all
what_happened: layer one turns a word into its address or into a glyph and writes nothing; layer two writes the words layer one could not resolve, once each, and it is the only place the table grows

rule: the reader sees a whole compiled line either way
why: a refusal at the input loses the output; refusing at the write keeps the reader's work visible and costs one condition
what_happened: a word that is not English is not written and is not refused, so the line is still compiled and printed, and only the write is skipped

rule: one condition, in one layer, not in both
why: while it lived in the conversion it made a conversion fail for a reason that has nothing to do with converting
what_happened: the condition on what may be written lives in the writing layer and nowhere else

rule: three roles, and none of them does another's work
why: an architect writes the spec, a compiler checks and keeps, a reader executes
what_happened: I took on role 2 while checking role 3, and the check belonged to neither: I asked a weak model to read glyphs, which is role 1 given to a model that has role 3
source: one evening, three roles, the format holds both ways

rule: the glyphs are a cheap keeping, and the decoder a cheap access
why: the model is given the resolved words inside the glyph frame, and the decoding in the head is the waste that the decoder removes
what_happened: the model was given raw glyphs and spent three hundred seconds on them, which is exactly the cost the decoder exists to avoid
source: one evening, three roles, the format holds both ways

rule: a sign is looked up and a word is resolved, and never both
why: a sign is read from the dictionary and is never written back as ASCII; a word is taken from the address and that one is English again
what_happened: converting a sign back throws the role away, and a bracket that is only a bracket says nothing about what it brackets
source: one evening, three roles, the format holds both ways

rule: the dictionary is consulted and the spec is executed, apart
why: they are two blocks, and a model that has both as one text works through the dictionary and answers nothing
what_happened: the model was given both and answered with the keys of the dictionary instead of the line it was asked to read
source: one evening, three roles, the format holds both ways

rule: a test that checks a role is not the role
why: a reader is not given a reading test, and an architect's check is not a reading
what_happened: two of my checks were on role 3 while I meant to check role 2, and both produced results that belonged to nothing
source: one evening, three roles, the format holds both ways

rule: the reader's rules carried a number the compiler derived
why: the width was written down in the rules while the compiler computed it, and the rules went stale the same evening
what_happened: the third time a number copied out of the code rotted: compile-03 with twelve bits, the width in the compiler, and now the width in the rules for the reader
source: one evening, three roles, the format holds both ways

rule: a frame check that reads one line at a time reports a frame that spans two lines as two faults
why: the checker asks each line whether its own brackets hold, so an opening on one line and a closing on another are never seen as one frame, and both lines are wrong in opposite directions
what_happened: the plugin reported four faults in a .vibe file that was not broken: two lists written across several lines, each giving a false unclosed and a false unexpected close. NOT CONFIRMED as the whole cause. The old-format document is also a candidate and the two were not told apart, because the document was written against an earlier version of the language and its frames mean something else now. Two candidates, one of them certain and the other not ruled out
how_to_check: write one frame across two lines and one on a single line, and compare what the plugin says. This was not done, so the cause is not established
